about.title: Marysville Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Marysville is a small city, but its stores, apartment complexes, and older sidewalks along corridors like 10th Street and B Street see plenty of foot traffic every day. When a property owner lets a spill sit, ignores broken pavement, or ignores a lighting problem in a stairwell, someone eventually gets hurt. California law asks whether the owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard before your fall. That's why what happens in the minutes after you go down matters: photos of the spot, names of witnesses, and a written incident report can make or break a claim later. LawProactive isn't a law firm — we're a free service that puts you in touch with an independent Yuba County premises liability attorney who can look at what happened, figure out who's responsible, and explain your options. There's no cost to talk, and no fee unless your case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before You Talk to the Property Owner

items.title: Notice Has to Be Proven
items.desc: Under California law, you generally must show the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard and didn't fix or warn about it. An attorney knows how to dig up maintenance logs, prior complaints, or inspection records that establish that notice.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many stores and apartment complexes overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Getting a preservation letter out quickly can be the difference between having proof of the hazard and having nothing.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Shrink Your Recovery
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so an insurer may try to argue you weren't watching where you were going. An attorney can push back on that narrative and gather evidence that keeps the focus on the hazard itself.

items.question: I fell at a Marysville business — what should I do first?
items.answer: Get photos of the exact spot where you fell, including any spill, debris, or damage, before it gets cleaned up or fixed. Ask an employee to file an incident report and get the names of anyone who saw it happen. Then seek medical care, even if you think the injury is minor, since some injuries show up hours later.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in California?
items.answer: Generally you have two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit against a private property owner. If a government-owned property in Yuba County is involved, the deadline is much shorter and requires a separate claims process, so it's worth talking to an attorney sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly to blame for the fall?
items.answer: California's comparative fault rule means you can still recover damages even if you share some responsibility, though your recovery may be reduced by your percentage of fault. An attorney can help make sure the property owner's negligence, not your own footing, stays the focus of the claim.
